_comment: Every number that moves a score lives in this file. prior_weight is the research-grounded default and NEVER changes; current_weight is what scoring actually uses and drifts as src/reweight.js learns from the sit log. To reset the model, copy prior back over current (npm run reweight -- --reset).
_methodology: This model is grounded in GPS-collar research (Auburn, Penn State, Mississippi State) rather than the popular hunting-app consensus. That is a deliberate choice by Ben, not an oversight. The visible consequences: moon phase carries ZERO weight, cold fronts get no dedicated factor beyond a modest temperature term, and rain is modeled as an interaction with wind speed rather than on its own. A future reviewer should not 'fix' these back toward folklore without new evidence. See ANNUAL_REVIEW.md.
_pressureRecoveryNote: Days of rest after which a hunted stand has given back half its pressure penalty, i.e. where the curve crosses zero. An Oklahoma GPS study had bucks cutting movement when hunters arrived, staying down through the hunt, and starting to recover about three days later. Raise it if your deer seem to stay spooky longer than that; the whole curve stretches with it.

frontal._comment: Shape of the frontal-passage factor. tempDropFullF is the 24h temperature fall that counts as a full-strength front; pressureRiseFullHpa is the 24h rise that says the low has cleared; preFrontalCeiling caps the feeding-ahead case well below the post-frontal one.

_peakRutNote: Single source of truth for the entire rut curve. Regional estimates for Central NC peak breeding span roughly Nov 15-20 and vary by county and year. Ben had no contrary read from past seasons at kickoff (2026-09-18) and chose to log a season before shifting it. Change this one value and the whole curve moves with it.

rutCurve._comment: Day offsets from peakRutDate mapped to a base buck score before any weather/pressure modifiers. Linearly interpolated between anchors. This is a lockdown-aware curve, not a bell curve: it peaks during CHASING (-7 to -2) and dips at peak breeding, because dominant bucks paired with an estrous doe go quiet for a day or two. Raw sightings drop right when 'the rut is peaking'.
rutCurve._generalNote: Flatter by design. General activity is driven by food, water and pressure far more than by rut phase. The December rise is late-season food concentration, not rut.

phases.label: Early pre-rut
phases.blurb: Bucks still in bachelor-ish patterns, movement slightly above baseline. Food patterns still hold.

phases.label: Seeking
phases.blurb: Daylight cruising climbs hard. Bucks covering ground checking doe groups. Best stretch to hunt travel between bedding and food.

phases.label: Chasing
phases.blurb: Most sustained daylight buck movement of the season. If you take one block of PTO, take it here.

phases.label: Peak breeding / lockdown
phases.blurb: Paired bucks go quiet with an estrous doe, so sightings drop off the chasing peak. Movement stays elevated but erratic as younger and subordinate bucks keep searching. Odd hours matter; midday is live.

phases.label: Post-rut lull
phases.blurb: The hardest stretch of the season. Bucks worn down and recovering, back on food but mostly after dark.

phases.label: Late post-rut
phases.blurb: Slow recovery. Food sources start concentrating deer again as cold sets in.

phases.label: Second rut
phases.blurb: Modest secondary bump from unbred does and doe fawns cycling, centered near day +28. Most hunters have written the season off by now, which is part of why it works.

phases.label: Late season
phases.blurb: Pure food-and-weather hunting. Cold snaps push midday and evening feeding.

rutCurve._calibrationNote: Anchors are BASE scores, not final scores. Factor contributions are added on top and bounded by factorSwing below, so a chasing-week base of 7.0 lands between roughly 4.5 on a warm wet pressured morning and 9.5 on a cold still one. If you retune these anchors, re-run 'npm run score -- --calibrate' and check the distribution still spreads across the 0-10 range instead of pinning at the top.

timeOfDay._comment: Score points added by slot, keyed to rut phase. AM wins during rut-driven cruising; PM wins when the hunt is food-driven. Baseline outside the listed phases is in 'default'.
timeOfDay._generalBiasNote: Added on top of the phase value for the general-activity score only. Does and young deer are more reliably an evening-food proposition than mature bucks are.

precipitation.label: Precipitation
precipitation.research: Penn State GPS-collar work: bucks cut movement by roughly half on rainy days. Does did not show the same response, which is why the buck weight is more than double the general weight. The same research found strong wind increases buck movement regardless of rain, so this factor models rain AND wind together, not rain alone.
precipitation.note: The single most reliable weather effect in the literature. Do not weaken this without a strong reason.

huntingPressure.label: Hunting pressure
huntingPressure.research: Not from the collar studies above. Pattern-avoidance in pressured deer is well established independently. Computed PER STAND from days since that stand was last hunted, so a stand untouched all season scores differently from one you sat on Tuesday.
huntingPressure.note: This is the factor you control. It is also the reason the sit log matters even before reweighting has enough data to run. The general weight is higher than the buck weight because pressure flattens overall sightings faster than it flattens rut-driven buck movement: a rutting buck will still cross a pressured stand chasing a doe, while the doe groups simply relocate.

foodProximity.label: Food proximity
foodProximity.research: Distance from the stand to the nearest marked food point. Scaled up by drought severity: when mast and browse fail, the remaining food concentrates deer harder than in a normal year.

waterProximity.label: Water proximity
waterProximity.research: Distance from the stand to the nearest water point that is still marked ACTIVE. Dry-flagged water contributes nothing. Scaled up by drought severity, and in a normal-rainfall year this factor nearly disappears, which is correct: water is not a limiting resource in the Piedmont most years.

tempDeparture.label: Temp departure from normal
tempDeparture.research: CONTESTED. Hunting-content sources treat cold fronts and temperature as the dominant predictor; the GPS-collar synthesis found minimal measured effect on overall movement distance. Weighted modestly as a compromise.
tempDeparture.note: Flagged as the best candidate for the reweighting system to move. It has the least research consensus of anything in this model, so Ben's own data should be allowed to speak loudest here.

tempChange24h.label: Temperature drop
tempChange24h.research: Change in temperature versus the same slot 24 hours earlier. A falling thermometer, especially the first cold morning behind a front, is the single most widely reported movement trigger in hunting practice. Note the tension this factor sits in: the GPS-collar synthesis this model is otherwise built on found temperature had minimal measured effect on total movement DISTANCE. Those are not quite the same claim, since a hunter cares about daylight visibility near food rather than distance covered, but the disagreement is real and unresolved.
tempChange24h.note: Added at Ben's request with a deliberately substantial prior, because he rates it highly from experience and the literature does not rule it out. It is flagged as a reweight candidate so his own sit log settles it rather than either of us asserting an answer. This is distinct from tempDeparture: departure asks 'is today warm for November', this asks 'did it just get colder'. A 45F morning can be both above normal and 15 degrees colder than yesterday.

pressureTrend.label: Barometric trend
pressureTrend.research: 24-hour change in sea-level pressure, in hectopascals, falling read as positive. Now measured from real data: previously this factor was fed by the NWS gridpoint pressure series, which returns unit 'None' with values near zero and was silently contributing nothing in 0 of 168 slots. Pressure now comes from Open-Meteo, which publishes genuine hPa hourly out 16 days.
pressureTrend.note: Weight raised modestly from 0.25 now that the input is real rather than absent. The research position stands: pressure largely tracks temperature rather than acting independently, so this should not be leaned on and will partly double-count tempChange24h. Reweighting can separate them once there is data, since the two do diverge - a cold front with a flat barometer happens.

frontalPassage.label: Frontal passage
frontalPassage.research: The conjunction of a cold drop and a recovering barometer, which is the clear cold morning after a low moves through. Scored separately because tempChange24h and pressureTrend each see one half of a front and actively disagree about this case: a post-frontal morning has a RISING barometer, which pressureTrend reads as negative. Also catches the pre-frontal case, a barometer dropping hard while it is still mild, at a much lower ceiling because that half rests largely on hunter consensus rather than collar data.
frontalPassage.note: One-sided by design: 0 to 1, never negative. The absence of a front is ordinary weather, not a penalty. It necessarily overlaps the two factors it is built from, so expect reweighting to move credit between the three once there are enough sits. If it has to lose, this is the one that should.

cloudCover.label: Cloud cover
cloudCover.research: Minor weight. Mainly relevant for extending usable low-light activity at the edges of legal light, not as a primary driver of whether deer move.

moonIllumination.label: Moon illumination
moonIllumination.research: Deliberately ZERO. Multiple independent studies, including the Mississippi State Deer Lab's 48-collar study, found no measurable effect of moon phase on deer movement, and specifically none for the 'moon overhead/underfoot' solunar theory. Moon phase and illumination are shown in the UI because Ben wants the reference point, but they do not move the number.
moonIllumination.note: Frozen by default: reweighting reports what it WOULD have fitted but does not write it. Without this, random noise across 40 sits is enough to nudge a zero-prior factor to the minAbsoluteDrift floor, which contradicts the whole reason moon is weighted zero. If several seasons of data ever show a consistent, sizeable moon effect, unfreeze it deliberately during the annual review rather than letting it creep in on noise. The fitted value is still shown in the reweighting report every run, so a real signal would be visible long before anyone acts on it.

_droughtBoostNote: Effective weight for drought-scaled factors = weight * (1 + droughtBoost * drought.severity). At the 2026 severity of 0.75 that is a 1.6x multiplier on food and water.

windRainInteraction._comment: Implements the 'strong winds increase buck movement no matter what' finding. Below cancelStartMph rain suppresses movement fully; between cancelStart and cancelFull the suppression fades out; above cancelFull the effect flips slightly positive.

reweighting._shrinkageNote: shrinkage = n / (n + 20). Ten logged sits gets about a third weight on the data, sixty gets about three-quarters. Standard empirical Bayes: the prior only yields as fast as the evidence earns it.
reweighting._driftNote: No factor may move more than 20% from its prior in one season. A dozen noisy sits from one property should not be able to swing the model.
reweighting._minDriftNote: Floor on the drift clip so factors with a zero or near-zero prior (moon) are not mathematically frozen at their prior forever. Deviation from the literal spec, documented in README.
reweighting._separationNote: If the high and low buckets barely differ in the factor's own effect value, the division that fits a weight blows up. Skip the factor instead.
reweighting._conversionNote: A 100-percentage-point swing in sighting rate between buckets is treated as worth 4.0 score points. This is the one frankly arbitrary constant in the reweighting math; it sets how aggressively observed sighting differences translate into weight changes.

scoreScale._comment: Scores are compressed toward the ends of the scale rather than hard-clamped. Above softKneeHigh the remaining headroom is allocated through a tanh curve, so a genuinely exceptional slot still ranks above a merely excellent one instead of both reading 10.0. Same in reverse below softKneeLow. The curve is monotonic, so this never changes the ORDER of two days, only the spacing between them near the extremes.

_calibrationNote: Affine map from the raw weighted sum onto the visible 0-10 scale: score = clamp((raw + offset) * gain, 0, 10). Identity until you run 'npm run score -- --calibrate', which simulates the whole season across a realistic spread of weather and fits offset/gain so the 5th percentile lands near 2 and the 95th near 9. Re-run it whenever the map changes materially (new stands, a pond going dry) or the drought severity changes, because both shift the raw range. Calibration changes what the numbers LOOK like, never how days rank against each other.

calibrationLimits._comment: Hard cap on calibration gain. If the raw scores genuinely do not spread far, the honest answer is a compressed visible range, not amplification. Stretching a 2.7-point raw spread across the full 0-10 scale makes a half-degree temperature difference look like the difference between a good sit and a bad one. When the cap binds, the score simply uses less of the scale, which is itself information: it means that score does not vary much on this property.

weatherDerivatives._comment: Windows for the change-based factors. 24 hours compares a slot against the same slot yesterday, which is the comparison a hunter actually makes. tempDropFullEffectF is the drop that produces a full +1 effect; pressureDropFullEffectHpa likewise.

windConfidence._comment: Gates the scent verdict. Below calmFloorMph thermals decide where scent goes and the forecast bearing means little; at reliableMph and above a steady wind can be trusted. Verdicts computed below minConfidenceForVerdict are reported as unreliable rather than given a safe/caution/blown answer, because a confident wrong answer on a calm morning is worse than no answer.
